text: This section answers whether the simulation completed, how its growth phenotype compares with the condition-matched wildtype when available, and whether the plotted curves are extracted from a completed run.
Time from simulated cell birth to division. Compare this with doubling time: division is a discrete cell-cycle event, while doubling time is calculated from growth rate.
Final simulated cell mass. Large changes can indicate broad biomass allocation effects even when division still occurs.
Specific growth rate near the end of the simulation. This is often the first phenotype to compare against WT.
Mass-doubling estimate from growth rate. It can differ from observed division time when the simulated cell cycle and biomass growth are not perfectly aligned.
Presets choose a small set of simulation channels for a specific interpretation task. You can still toggle individual channels; doing so creates a custom view.

Advanced output-series search. Search by gene symbol, EcoCyc ID, protein, metabolite, reaction, or raw output ID. Counts below are plottable simulation output series, not unique biological molecules.
plottable output series for this cell —

Per-cell count of distinct plottable series — not a total across seeds, generations, or other runs (it's the same for every result). It exceeds the number of distinct biological molecules because mRNA is offered at both transcription-unit and gene/cistron level, and reversible reactions appear as forward+reverse fluxes. Plotting one molecule returns one trajectory per cell lineage (seeds × generations).
